# Projects

## Health Risk Modeling Analysis

Investigated whether physical food access or socioeconomic factors better explain chronic health outcomes across Lancaster County, Nebraska. Found that educational attainment was a substantially stronger predictor of obesity than proximity to grocery stores — a result that held across both linear and nonlinear models.

**Tools:** Python, pandas, scikit-learn, geopandas  
**Data:** ACS (U.S. Census Bureau), CDC PLACES, OpenStreetMap  

[View Report (PDF)](files/Math_in_the_City___Group_4__Spring_2026.pdf){target="_blank"}

<details>
<summary>See technical details</summary>

- Engineered distance-based and density features from OpenStreetMap using OSMnx (distance to nearest grocery store, fast food density per km²)
- Built multiple linear regression model achieving R² ≈ 0.49; compared against random forest (R² ≈ 0.59)
- Feature importance analysis confirmed percent without a high school diploma (importance: 0.721) as the dominant predictor over physical food access (0.143)
- Performed 5-fold cross-validation to evaluate model stability across tract subsets
- Visualized spatial clustering of obesity, poverty, and transit access across census tracts using geopandas

</details>

## Deep Learning Projects

Built and evaluated neural network models for text and image classification tasks, comparing architectures and tuning for performance.

**Tools:** Python, TensorFlow, Keras, scikit-learn  

[View Example Report (PDF)](files/CSCE479879Homework3.pdf){target="_blank"}

<details>
<summary>See technical details</summary>

- **Sentiment Analysis** — sequential model for text classification; preprocessed and tokenized input data
- **SVHN Classification** — convolutional neural network for street-view digit recognition
- **Fashion MNIST** — fully connected architecture; benchmarked against alternative configurations
- Tuned hyperparameters and evaluated models using accuracy and loss metrics across all three tasks

</details>
